items.snippet: All three rear cameras use 200-megapixel sensors. | Image: Oppo Oppo's new Find X10 Pro Max flagship phone, launched today in China, is the first anywhere to use 200-megapixel sensors on all three of its rear cameras. A 17-stop dynamic range for the main camera, delivered thanks to what Oppo calls "DeepPix sensor technology," suggests megapixel count won't be the only thing this camera has going for it - a good thing, since raw resolution hasn't been the main driver of smartphone image quality for some time. The triple rear camera is built into a square, raised camera island, with a separate bar to one side holding the flash and an additional sensor. An orange accent line nods to Oppo's ongo

items.title: Vivo’s X500 Pro Max has 17 stops of dynamic range and 4K240 slo-mo
items.snippet: All three new X500 phones support at least one of Vivo’s teleconverter lenses. | Image: Vivo Vivo's new X500 flagship phones have arrived in China, and as usual the company's focus is firmly on photography. The X500 Pro Max - a new tier in its lineup - is the first phone to use new sensors and silicon from Sony and MediaTek that enable impressive dynamic range and slow-motion video recording. The X500 Pro Max uses Sony's new Lytia L910 image sensor , its first to use LOFIC, a sensor technology that enables expanded dynamic range. The 50-megapixel, 1/1.28-inch-type sensor delivers what Vivo calls "true 17 EV ultra-high dynamic range," more than the 16.5 stops claimed by the Xiaomi 17 Ultra .

items.title: Apple Planning to Bring iPhone Duo Display Tech to Pro in 2029
items.snippet: Apple's 2029 "Pro" iPhones could adopt thinner and more power-efficient OLED screens, according to UBI Research . The technology, known as Color Filter on Encapsulation (CoE), removes the conventional polarizer from the ‌OLED‌ panel and places a color filter directly on top of its encapsulation layer. A polarizer helps suppress reflections from ambient light, but it also absorbs a significant portion of the light produced by the display. Removing the polarizer allows more light to pass through, potentially enabling a display to reach greater brightness without consuming additional power, or use less power while maintaining the same brightness. items.title: watchOS 27.2 beta 2 brings the App Switcher back with a new gesture
items.snippet: If you’ve been missing the double-click of the Digital Crown that used to bring up the App Switcher on the Apple Watch before watchOS 27, it looks like the feature is making a comeback as of watchOS 27.2 beta 2. Here are the details. Earlier today, Apple rolled out watchOS 27.2 beta 2 for developers, less than a week after releasing beta 1. Included in today’s beta is a tidbit that will likely please longtime Apple Watch users, including my colleague Zac Hall. Earlier this month, he wrote about how watchOS 27 had removed the ability to quickly switch between recently used apps by double-clicking the Digital Crown. items.snippet: Macworld USB-C is the modern connection standard shared by most new devices today. It comes in several different formats—USB-C, USB4 and Thunderbolt—but they all have the same reversible connector at the end and are interchangeable and backwards compatible. The technical disclosure is now public, while patches released on August 11 are already available for SharePoint Server 2016, 2019, and Subscription Edition. Source

items.title: Critical Linux ARM64 KVM flaw leaves host memory writable from a guest
items.snippet: Researchers have disclosed CVE-2026-89775, a critical flaw in the Linux kernel’s ARM64 KVM virtualization code. When nested virtualization is enabled, a guest can read and write freed host memory, creating a potential guest-to-host escape. Administrators should patch to Linux 6.18.51, 7.2.5, or 7.3-rc1, or verify that the experimental nested-virtualization feature is disabled. Source

items.title: BigDiskBuster fills disks to freeze Microsoft Defender updates
items.snippet: A new BigDiskBuster proof of concept can prevent Microsoft Defender from installing platform and security intelligence updates by temporarily consuming all available disk space. The tool leaves Defender running but can keep its protection content stuck at older versions; no Microsoft patch, CVE, or advisory is currently available. Source

items.title: When you type bbc.com, the browser may trigger several invisible network exchanges: it asks a DNS resolver for the site's address, opens a TCP connection with three packets, negotiates encryption keys, and only then requests the page, with each uncached round trip adding delay
